correctness.rationale: A unitary Fourier conjugate of the contrast projection is a positive orthogonal projector of trace n-1 with zero row sums after translating one excluded point to identity. Rowwise triangle gives Fourier l1 mass at least 2(n-1). Equality forces all offdiagonals to be nonpositive real, so the Fourier matrix is a weighted Laplacian whose kernel contains every excluded coordinate character. Restriction to the subgroup generated by excluded labels makes distinct character fibers orthogonal, and the within-fiber row-sum formula yields |S_B(phi)|^2=n(h-m) for all nontrivial phi. Parseval on the subgroup forces h=m, hence subgroup labels. Conversely subgroup labels make all offdiagonals nonpositive. All quantifiers are finite and algebraic; 3910 complete small-case numerical tests corroborate but are not used as proof.

value.rationale: The problem is the natural Fourier l1 norm of a coordinate mean-zero orthogonal projector, and it is exactly the harmonic complexity of the unbalanced complete-bipartite eigenvalue-m sector. The result doubles the previously generic multiplicity lower bound, proves a sharp arithmetic if-and-only-if criterion across all abelian labeling groups, and classifies every equality configuration. It gives a structural, infinite-family answer to the subgroup-attainment portion of a 2026 explicitly stated open question, not a finite table or superficial parameter specialization. The nondivisible exact minimum remains open.
